root_cause.text: The microchip-core-qspi driver left the controller’s single built-in chip select in hardware-automatic mode, so any transfer started on the bus could assert that CS even when Linux was communicating with a different SPI device selected via GPIO.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states “if there are two devices attached to this QSPI controller … the in-built chip select is set low while linux tries to access the device attached to the GPIO,” and the patch fixes this by enabling software-controlled CS via `DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL`, adding `mchp_coreqspi_set_cs()`, wiring `ctlr->set_cs`, and explicitly asserting/deasserting CS around `exec_op()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add symbolic QSPI Direct Access register bit definitions to support future direct access register handling.
intent_record.what: A new comment block and three preprocessor macros were added for QSPI Direct Access register fields: DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL as BIT(0), DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL as BIT(1), and DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL_SHIFT as 1.
intent_record.how: This introduces named constants for direct access register bit definitions, enabling subsequent code to reference these fields symbolically instead of using raw bit values, but it does not change runtime behavior by itself in the shown hunk.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add explicit chip-select control and initialize active-low CS lines inactive during setup to avoid unintended device selection.
intent_record.what: The change adds two new functions: `mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(struct spi_device *spi, bool enable)`, which reads `REG_DIRECT_ACCESS`, clears `DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL`, sets it according to `!enable << DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL_SHIFT`, and writes the value back; and `mchp_coreqspi_setup(struct spi_device *spi)`, which for devices not using `SPI_CS_HIGH` reads `REG_DIRECT_ACCESS`, sets `DIRECT_ACCESS_OP_SSEL`, writes it back, and returns 0, while returning immediately for `SPI_CS_HIGH` devices.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this adds explicit chip-select line control through the direct access register and initializes active-low chip-select devices to their inactive state during setup/probe, preventing them from being left asserted unintentionally before transfers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove the dedicated operation-setup helper that configured the control register, likely consolidating that setup logic elsewhere.
intent_record.what: The diff removes the entire static function mchp_coreqspi_setup_op(), which previously retrieved the controller and driver data from a spi_device, read the REG_CONTROL register, set CONTROL_MASTER and CONTROL_ENABLE, cleared CONTROL_CLKIDLE, wrote the updated value back, and returned 0.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates that helper routine, so this file no longer provides a dedicated operation-setup function that explicitly enables master mode, enables the controller, and forces the clock-idle bit low through that code path. Runtime behavior would only remain the same if equivalent register configuration is now performed elsewhere; otherwise this setup step is no longer executed via this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Assert chip select before starting a QSPI memory operation so commands are issued with the device properly selected.
intent_record.what: A call to mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, true); was inserted in mchp_coreqspi_exec_op() immediately after mchp_coreqspi_config_op(qspi, op) and before processing op->cmd.opcode.
intent_record.how: This actively asserts the chip select line before executing the SPI memory operation, ensuring the target device is selected when command/data transfer begins and preventing transactions from starting without CS being asserted.

intent_record.intent_summary: Deassert chip select in the QSPI operation error path to avoid leaving CS asserted after failures.
intent_record.what: A call to mchp_coreqspi_set_cs(mem->spi, false); was added in the error: path of mchp_coreqspi_exec_op(), immediately before mutex_unlock(&qspi->op_lock) and mchp_coreqspi_disable_ints(qspi).
intent_record.how: This ensures the SPI chip select is explicitly deasserted when execution reaches the error handling path, preventing CS from remaining asserted after a failed or timed-out operation and restoring the device/bus to a sane state.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add local 32-bit variables in mchp_coreqspi_probe() to support upcoming probe-time configuration handling.
intent_record.what: In the local variable declarations of mchp_coreqspi_probe(), a new declaration was added so that two 32-bit variables, num_cs and val, are defined alongside the existing int ret.
intent_record.how: This change by itself does not alter runtime behavior in the shown hunk, but it prepares the probe function to store and use 32-bit values later in the function, likely for controller configuration or device-tree-derived parameters such as chip select count.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the CoreQSPI probe path to honor device-tree-defined chip select count, default to one native CS, and avoid using the old setup callback.
intent_record.what: The probe function now reads the device tree property "num-cs" into a local variable, defaults it to 1 if the property is absent, assigns that value to ctlr->num_chipselect, and adds a comment explaining that the IP core has only one native chip select and additional chip selects must come from GPIOs; it also removes the assignment ctlr->setup = mchp_coreqspi_setup_op.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SPI controller now advertises a configurable number of chip selects based on device tree data instead of implicitly relying on a single default, allowing extra chip selects to be represented when provided externally via GPIOs. Removing the custom setup callback stops that per-device setup path from being used.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize the CoreQSPI controller in enabled master mode and switch chip select to software-controlled handling via SPI callbacks during probe.
intent_record.what: The probe function stops assigning ctlr->num_chipselect = 2 and instead assigns ctlr->setup = mchp_coreqspi_setup and ctlr->set_cs = mchp_coreqspi_set_cs, then adds register initialization code before spi_register_controller() to read REG_CONTROL, set CONTROL_MASTER and CONTROL_ENABLE bits, write it back, read REG_DIRECT_ACCESS, set DIRECT_ACCESS_EN_SSEL, and write it back with a comment indicating chip select is put into software-controlled mode.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the SPI controller is now explicitly initialized into enabled master mode during probe and configured so chip select is driven through software control via the controller's set_cs callback, rather than relying only on a fixed num_chipselect setting. This enables proper controller setup and chip-select handling needed for SPI device communication.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix QSPI chip-select handling by explicitly controlling CS during initialization and memory operations, including proper assert/deassert behavior on start and error paths.

relevance_review.reason: This change only adds symbolic register bit definitions for future direct-access handling and does not modify chip-select behavior or address the controller being left in automatic CS mode.

The changes directly address incorrect QSPI chip-select behavior by taking explicit control of CS, initializing it to an inactive state, asserting it only for intended memory operations, and deasserting it on errors. This matches the root cause of the controller leaving its built-in CS in automatic mode and unintentionally selecting the wrong device.

The described change removes/refactors an operation-setup helper for control register configuration, but it does not specifically indicate fixing the chip-select mode issue where the built-in CS remained in automatic hardware mode and interfered with GPIO-selected devices.
Adding local 32-bit variables in probe() for future configuration handling does not by itself address the chip-select hardware-automatic mode issue or prevent incorrect CS assertion during transfers.

The root cause is incorrect handling of the controller’s built-in chip select. This change updates probe-time chip-select configuration to respect device-tree CS count, default correctly to one native CS, and stop relying on the old setup path, which directly affects how the native hardware CS is managed and helps prevent the unintended assertion issue.

The change directly addresses the root cause by moving the controller’s chip select away from hardware-automatic behavior to software-controlled SPI callback handling during probe, preventing unintended assertion of the built-in CS during transfers to other devices.

candidates.rationale: The old setup callback was removed by the fix because chip select needed to be handled explicitly via message callbacks/software control. Leaving this setup path in place contributed to relying on hardware-automatic native CS behavior instead of safe explicit CS management.

Advertising two chip selects while the hardware has a single built-in native CS enabled the controller to be used with another device selected through GPIO, but the native hardware CS could still be asserted automatically during transfers, creating the unintended dual-selection condition described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This probe-time initialization advertised support for two chip selects even though the controller has a single built-in native CS that remained in hardware-automatic mode. That made it possible to use another SPI device via GPIO chip select while transfers could still automatically assert the native CS, causing the unintended dual-selection condition described in the root cause.

Keeping the old setup callback in the probe path reflects the pre-fix design that relied on the controller's default/native chip-select handling rather than switching to explicit software-controlled CS management. In the vulnerable state, probe did not reconfigure the built-in CS out of automatic mode before the controller was used.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 8f9cf02c8852837923f1cdacfcc92e138513325c
Author: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 20 14:28:26 2025 +0100

    spi: microchip-core-qspi: Add regular transfers
    
    The driver for CoreQSPI only supports memory operations at present, so
    add support for regular transfers so that the SD card slot and ADC on
    the BeagleV Fire can be used.
    
    Signed-off-by: Cyril Jean <cyril.jean@microchip.com>
    Co-developed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the newly added regular-transfer path, message preparation, and controller registration details relevant to chip-select behavior. The vulnerable condition is present: this commit enables regular SPI transfers by adding `prepare_message`, `transfer_one`, and setting `ctlr->num_chipselect = 2;` plus `ctlr->use_gpio_descriptors = true;`, which allows multiple logical devices including GPIO-based CS. However, nowhere in the shown code is the hardware controller's built-in chip select switched to a safe/manual/disabled state for regular transfers. In `mchp_coreqspi_prepare_message()`, the code programs clock, mode, and frame registers (`REG_CONTROL`, `REG_FRAMESUP`, `REG_FRAMES`) but does not configure chip-select handling based on `m->spi->chip_select` or prevent automatic assertion of the internal CS. `mchp_coreqspi_transfer_one()` similarly only pushes TX/RX data and has no CS management. Thus the vulnerable construct exists: regular transfers are introduced while the controller may still automatically assert its single built-in CS, which can conflict with Linux using a GPIO CS for another device. The fix is not present because there is no logic here to force the hardware CS into non-automatic mode or otherwise gate it to only the intended native-CS device.

    Add a driver for Microchip FPGA QSPI controllers. This driver also
    supports "hard" QSPI controllers on Polarfire SoC.
    
    Signed-off-by: Naga Sureshkumar Relli <nagasuresh.relli@microchip.com>
    Reviewed-by: Conor Dooley <conor.dooley@microchip.com>
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it shows the controller setup/probe logic and all register programming related to transfer enablement, and there is no handling of chip-select mode anywhere in the new driver. The root cause is leaving the controller's built-in CS in hardware-automatic mode so transfers can assert it even when Linux uses a different GPIO CS. In this commit, `mchp_coreqspi_setup_op()` only does `control |= (CONTROL_MASTER | CONTROL_ENABLE);` and `control &= ~CONTROL_CLKIDLE;` before writing `REG_CONTROL`; there is no code to switch the internal CS to software/manual or otherwise disable automatic hardware CS behavior. Likewise, `mchp_coreqspi_probe()` registers the controller and sets `ctlr->mode_bits`, `ctlr->setup`, and `ctlr->mem_ops`, but does not configure any chip-select behavior, and the driver does not advertise or manage `num_chipselect` / GPIO-vs-native CS interaction. Since the vulnerable construct is the absence of explicit disabling/manual control of the built-in hardware CS, and that absence is present throughout this function set, the bug is present and the fix is not yet included.
